subject: Science
focus: Understanding Magnetism Through Observation and Experimentation
source_reference: NCERT Class 6 Science Chapter 4 – Exploring Magnets

foundation.concept_text: Some materials stick to a magnet, while others do not.

standard.concept_text: Materials that are attracted towards a magnet are called magnetic materials. Materials not attracted are called non-magnetic materials.

advanced.concept_text: Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials. Magnetism depends on the internal structure of materials.

activity.title: Testing Materials with a Magnet
steps: Collect objects made of wood, plastic, iron, glass and rubber.
Predict which objects will stick to a magnet.
Test each object and record observations.
activity.expected_learning: Students understand that magnets attract only specific materials.

images.title: Different Shapes of Magnets
images.instructional_purpose: Show bar, U-shaped and ring magnets

foundation.concept_text: A magnet has two ends called poles.

standard.concept_text: The two ends of a magnet are called North pole and South pole. Maximum magnetic strength is at the poles.

advanced.concept_text: Magnetic poles always exist in pairs. A single pole cannot exist even if the magnet is broken.

activity.title: Iron Filings Experiment
steps: Spread iron filings on a sheet of paper.
Place a bar magnet over the filings.
activity.expected_learning: Students observe magnetic strength concentration at poles.

images.title: Iron Filings Around Bar Magnet
images.instructional_purpose: Show clustering of filings at poles

micro_lessons.title: Finding Directions and the Magnetic Compass

foundation.concept_text: A freely suspended magnet comes to rest in the north-south direction.

standard.concept_text: The end pointing north is called the North-seeking pole. The Earth behaves like a giant magnet.

advanced.concept_text: The magnetic compass works because its needle is a freely rotating magnet aligned by Earth’s magnetic field.

activity.title: Making a Simple Compass
steps: Magnetize an iron needle by stroking it with a bar magnet.
Insert the needle into a cork.

foundation.concept_text: Magnets can attract or repel each other.

standard.concept_text: Unlike poles attract each other, while like poles repel each other.

advanced.concept_text: Repulsion is the sure test of magnetism because iron can be attracted but cannot repel.

activity.title: Interaction Between Two Magnets
steps: Bring another magnet close without touching.
